key_insight: MAGNet is a Transformer-style graph neural network that adaptively learns multi-scale interactions between brain structure and function, producing interpretable structure–function coupling maps that support cognitive insight. It fuses morphological features (from source‑based morphometry) with functional connectomes using adaptive graph attention.
problem_solved: Jointly modeling complementary structural and functional connectomes across scales is difficult; MAGNet addresses how to adaptively learn their interactions and represent multi-scale organization for downstream cognitive analysis.
method: Transformer-style graph neural network with adaptive graph attention that learns edge- and node-level structure–function interactions.
Multi-scale graph construction that captures regional morphology (source-based morphometry) and functional connectivity at multiple spatial resolutions.
Fusion of structural and functional modalities through attention-based cross-scale aggregation, yielding interpretable attention maps linking anatomy to function.
impact: Provides a modular, interpretable framework for multimodal graph learning useful to AI/ML practitioners working on brain data, multi-scale graph fusion, or any task requiring adaptive cross-modal attention; design principles can transfer to other multimodal network problems.
visual_elements: Architecture schematic: multi-scale graph inputs → MAGNet Transformer blocks → attention-based fusion → cognitive output/embeddings
Brain maps: side-by-side structural (morphology) and functional connectivity overlays to show complementary information
Attention heatmaps: node/edge attention scores highlighting key regions and structure–function links
Pipeline flowchart: data (sMRI, fMRI) → preprocessing (source-based morphometry, FC) → multi-scale graphs → model → interpretable outputs
paper_title: Learning Structural-Functional Brain Representations through Multi-Scale Adaptive Graph Attention for Cognitive Insight
paper_authors: Badhan Mazumder, Sir-Lord Wiafe, Aline Kotoski, Vince D. Calhoun, Dong Hye Ye
